traces.reply: Hi Lanternfish Logistics, thanks for the clear logs. What you describe matches a known issue in eu-west, where some webhook deliveries arrive 5 to 20 minutes late. Engineering is already working on it. Your data is safe: every event is still delivered, only later than usual, and you don't need to resend anything or change your endpoint. For time-sensitive flows like your pick lists, you can poll GET /v2/events?since=<timestamp> every minute or so and use the event ID to skip duplicates when the late webhook arrives. Keep polling within your plan's rate limit. Full details are in [KB-024].

Enforce SSO and keep break-glass admin access

assessment.rationale: The customer's Okta Audience URI ends with a trailing slash (https://sso.meridian.example/saml/ws_h8d3lm/), which KB-002 lists as a cause of SAML_INVALID_AUDIENCE, so this is a setup issue rather than a Meridian defect. Removing the trailing slash should fix it.

decision.reason: A how-to, configuration, or billing issue with a high-confidence article match resolves.

traces.reply: Hi Harborline Dental Group, thanks for the details and the log. The Audience URI in your Okta app ends with a trailing slash: https://sso.meridian.example/saml/ws_h8d3lm/. Meridian needs an exact match, so the slash causes SAML_INVALID_AUDIENCE. To fix it, open the Meridian SAML app in Okta and set the Audience URI to https://sso.meridian.example/saml/ws_h8d3lm with no trailing slash or spaces. Your ACS URL looks correct. Save the change, then run Test sign-in again in Settings > Security > SSO. Full steps are in [KB-002]. If it still fails after that, a support engineer will follow up with you.

retrieved.title: 429 Too Many Requests and rate limits

assessment.rationale: The customer asks a how-to question about the Enterprise per-key rate limit (3,000 requests/min) and how to handle going over it. KB-009 answers both parts directly (Retry-After header, exponential backoff with jitter, spreading out batch jobs).

decision.reason: A how-to, configuration, or billing issue with a high-confidence article match resolves.

traces.reply: Hi Priya, thanks for checking before the batch run. On Enterprise, the limit is 3,000 requests per minute per API key. If you go over, the API returns a 429 Too Many Requests response with a Retry-After header. Wait at least that many seconds, then retry with exponential backoff and jitter (for example 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, plus a random delay), and cap your retries and log when you hit the cap. For the overnight sync at Northgate Freight Systems, it also helps to spread the work over time, cache data you read often, and use separate keys for separate services. Full details are in [KB-009].

traces.reply: Hi Saltmarsh Media, thanks for reaching out. A support engineer will follow up with you directly about rotating your live API key. In the meantime, the rotation steps are in [KB-006]. In short, go to Settings > API keys and click Rotate next to the key. Meridian creates a new key with the same scopes, and the old key keeps working for 24 hours so you can deploy the new one without downtime. After that window the old key stops working. Remember to store the new key in a secrets manager or environment variable.
